episode_title: Fight the “CF-No”: Anders Liu Lindenberg on Real Business Partnering

real_qa.q: What is the Business Partnering Institute formula for effective finance business partnering?
real_qa.r: Anders Liu Lindenberg defines business partnering as: insights times influence equal to impact. Insights are new perspectives that decision makers don't yet know but can help them make better decisions, coming from financials, non-financials, and conversations. Influence comes down to communication ability, relationships, and trust—if you are trusted, you are consulted on decisions rather than just informed. Together, insights and influence create impact by improving decisions and maximizing value creation.
real_qa.requete: Business Partnering Institute insights influence impact formula

real_qa.q: Why do finance professionals default to no instead of finding a path forward in business decisions?
real_qa.r: Anders explains that finance professionals often have a 99 percent mindset—they won't say anything unless 99 percent sure it's correct, which works for accounting and external reporting but not for internal planning and forward-looking statements where you can never be 99 percent certain. The issue is that decisions are made before finance gets involved because finance lacks influence and trust, not necessarily because they lack insights. By reframing questions from 'can I do this' to 'how can I do this,' business partners open up creativity and discover viable paths forward rather than defaulting to no.
real_qa.requete: why finance says no instead of how CF-No business partnering

real_qa.q: What is the communication gap between finance professionals and business leaders in financial reporting?
real_qa.r: Finance professionals often present complex management reports with huge tables full of columns, rows, numbers, deviation explanations, red-green colors and text that looks like Excel snippets, which few people understand or want to try understanding. Anders showed how one training participant transformed such a table into two simple slides with two columns, four rows, and three recommended action points that anyone can understand. The root problem is not that business leaders lack financial acumen, but that finance professionals struggle to communicate financials in simple, plain language that business leaders can grasp.
real_qa.requete: finance reporting communication excel tables business leaders

real_qa.q: When did Anders Liu Lindenberg start full-time with the Business Partnering Institute and what drove its growth?
real_qa.r: Anders started full-time with the Business Partnering Institute during COVID-19, before which he was doing marketing on the side. COVID forced everyone to move virtual, which meant learning programs could be delivered without gathering people in person. Coming out of summer 2020, there was massive demand for their services—he had made a sales plan for the first year and hit it almost entirely in the last six months of that year because companies everywhere needed to develop their people while in lockdown.
real_qa.requete: Business Partnering Institute COVID-19 growth Anders full-time 2020

real_qa.q: What is the training gap between importance and actual delivery of communication skills for finance professionals?
real_qa.r: When asked how important communication is to career success on a scale of one to ten, finance professionals say 9.5 on average. When asked how much training they have received in communication on the same scale, they say 4.5 on average. This five-point gap means finance professionals are not trained to actually succeed in the roles they are given today, which is why the Business Partnering Institute focuses heavily on soft skills training alongside business partnering development.

guest.bio_context: Anders Liu Lindenberg is a prolific author and LinkedIn influencer who co-founded the Business Partnering Institute. He spent 10 years becoming a business partner expert, working at companies including Merck and Maersk where he saw firsthand the need for structured training in finance business partnering. He transitioned to full-time consulting with the Business Partnering Institute during COVID-19, which accelerated demand for learning and development programs globally.
